html:
British Cyrenaica was eastern Libya under British military rule from 1943, after the desert war drove out the Italians, until Libya became independent in 1951.

Cyrenaica, around Benghazi and the Green Mountain, had suffered most under Italian rule. Its Sufi leaders of the Senusiyya had fought Italy for decades. In the Second World War their head, Idris al-Senussi, sided with Britain, and Libyan volunteers fought beside British troops in the Western Desert campaign.

Britain repaid him. In 1949 it let Idris declare an Emirate of Cyrenaica under British protection. When the United Nations ruled that Libya should be united and free, Idris became king of the new Kingdom of Libya in December 1951. He reigned until Muammar Gaddafi's coup in 1969.
sum: British Cyrenaica was eastern Libya under British military rule from 1943, after the desert war drove out the Italians, until Libya became independent in 1951.
